sentences.text:
1  THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 19.02.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.506/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE COURT OF THE PRL. SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM AND MEMBER OF MACT NO.V VIJAYAPUR AT VIJAYAPUR AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL TO GRANT THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.8,28,117/- ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BEFORE THIS HON'BLE COURT AND ETC.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation and also fixing the liability on the owner and thereby exonerating the insurance company from payment of compensation, appellant who is the petitioner before the Tribunal has come up with this appeal.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that on 26.01.2015 at about 2:30 p.m. he was proceeding towards Vijayapura on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-28-U-2508 (for short 'motorcycle').

When he was near Aliyabad- Vijayapura road, the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/EE-7199 (for short 'offending vehicle'), being driven by its rider in a rash or negligent manner came and dashed against the petitioner.
In the said accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability affecting his earning capacity.
As owner and insurer respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

5. Before the Tribunal respondent No.1 remained ex parte.
6.
Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement disputing the age, occupation, nature of injuries sustained and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability.
Respondent No.2 cannot be held liable unless and until it is proved that there is RC, FC and driver had valid driving licence and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

8. Petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and relied upon Exs.P1 to 8.
9.
On behalf of respondent No.2, R.W.1 is examined and Exs.R.1 to 6 are marked.

sentences.text: Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal partly allowed the petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.46,883/- with interest @ 9% p.a. and directed respondent No.1 to pay the same on the ground that at the time of accident, the rider of offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence.
The details of the compensation granted are detailed in the table:
Sl . No

. Heads Amount  1. Medical bills Rs.26,883/-
 2. Global compensation Rs.20,000/-
 Total Rs.46,883/-
 11.
Respondent No.1 has not challenged the impugned Judgment and award.
12. The petitioner is before this Court contending that having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered, the compensation granted is on the lower side.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu And Others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba And Another1 (Pappu's case), respondent No.2 is to be directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from respondent No.1.
13.

entities.text: Pappu And Others Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba And Another1 (Pappu's case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though duly served, respondent No.1 remained absent.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.

Appreciating the oral and documentary evidence placed on record and having regard to the fact that there is no disability affecting the earning capacity of the petitioner and taking into consideration the medical bills, for a sum of Rs.26,883/- produced by the petitioner, the Tribunal has granted global compensation in a sum of Rs.46,883/- including the medical bills.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to enhance the compensation by an additional sum of Rs.15,000/-.
However, the petitioner is not entitled for interest on the enhanced compensation.
17. Now coming to the question of liability.

It is an undisputed fact that as on the date of accident,
the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2.
However, the Tribunal has exonerated respondent No.2 from the liability on the ground that at the time of accident rider of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence.

However, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu's case, wherein it is held that when the offending vehicle is insured, in the absence of the driver of offending vehicle possessing a valid driving licence,
the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner.

sentences.text: Therefore, in this case also it is necessary to direct respondent No.2/insurance company to pay the compensation with interest and recover the same from respondent No.1-owner.

18. To this extent, the appeal deserves to be allowed and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellant/petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.61,883/-
together with interest at 6% per annum.
However, the petitioner is not entitled for interest on enhanced compensation of Rs.15,000/-.

(iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation together with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order and recover the same from respondent No.1.
(iv) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of this order.
Sd/-
